body_markdown:
This article compares two prescription treatment classes: a dual-receptor approach and a single-receptor approach. The two work through different biology, and understanding that difference is a useful starting point for how Health Canada has reviewed each, what clinical trial data shows, and what a provider weighs on safety before prescribing either. This article covers the mechanisms, approvals, research, and practical factors side by side, so you have a fuller picture before your next conversation with a provider.


**TLDR:**


- Tirzepatide acts on two hormone receptors (GIP and GLP-1); semaglutide targets GLP-1 alone.
- Health Canada reviews both through a formal process, publishing safety and quality findings for each.
- Nausea, diarrhea, constipation, and vomiting are common with both, especially during dose changes.
- A licensed provider weighs medical history, current prescriptions, and personal preference before considering either option.

## What Is Tirzepatide?


Tirzepatide is a prescription treatment classified as a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist. These are two separate hormone receptors: glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1).


### How Tirzepatide Is Administered


It is given as an injection under the skin. In Canada, tirzepatide is available through products approved by Health Canada for specific medical uses, and a licensed healthcare provider determines whether it fits a patient's health profile.


Working on two receptor types instead of one is simply a description of its mechanism, not a claim about results. Providers weigh medical history, current health, and treatment goals before considering this option.


## What Is Semaglutide?


Semaglutide is a prescription treatment classified as a GLP-1 receptor agonist. This is a single hormone receptor called glucagon-like peptide-1.


### Available Formats and Health Canada Authorization


In Canada, semaglutide is available in more than one prescription format, including an injection given under the skin and an oral tablet. Health Canada has authorized specific semaglutide products for defined medical uses, and a licensed healthcare provider reviews a patient's health history before determining whether either format is appropriate for that individual.


Working on one receptor type is a functional description, not an outcome claim. Suitability always depends on factors a provider assesses directly.


## Understanding Single and Dual Receptor Pathways


This treatment class activates a single pathway, the GLP-1 receptor, one of the hormone receptors involved in the body's digestive system.


### How a Dual Receptor Pathway Works


This treatment class activates two pathways, both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. GIP is a hormone that plays a general role in insulin regulation and fat metabolism, working alongside GLP-1 instead of replacing it. A StatPearls clinical reference on[dual receptor action](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK585056/) describes this combined activity as central to how the treatment functions.


### Factors a Provider Weighs


Neither pathway is classified as better than the other. Single versus dual receptor activity are different biological routes toward managing appetite signals and blood sugar, and the right fit depends on individual health history as determined by a licensed provider.

## Health Canada's Review Process for These Treatment Categories


### How Health Canada Reviewed Each Brand


Health Canada has reviewed both treatments through its formal process, publishing a Summary Basis of Decision for each that covers safety, effectiveness, and quality findings. The[decision summary for Mounjaro](https://dhpp.hpfb-dgpsa.ca/review-documents/resource/SBD00629) outlines this review. The summary is updated as new submissions or indications come through.


### Generic Semaglutide Authorization


On the generic side, Health Canada authorized a[generic semaglutide](https://www.phoenix.ca/medications/generic-semaglutide) injection for weight loss in 2026, with additional submissions reportedly under review at the time. This affects supply and access, not how the original brand products were reviewed. For a closer look at how[generic semaglutide compares to Ozempic and Wegovy](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/generic-semaglutide-vs-ozempic-bioequivalence-price) in Canada, bioequivalence and pricing are key factors to consider.


Neither authorization means regulators favor one treatment over the other. Both remain prescription-only and subject to change, so treat any approval detail here as a snapshot, not a permanent fact.


## What Does Clinical Research Say About These Treatment Categories?


Both treatment categories have been studied in randomized clinical trials that track measures related to weight and blood sugar control over several months. Reported outcomes differ depending on the study group, the dose used, and how long the trial ran, so figures from one trial should not be read as a direct stand-in for another.


Any numbers that come out of this kind of research are averages across a study group, not a forecast for what will happen to one person. A licensed healthcare provider looks at this research alongside a patient's own health history, current prescriptions, and goals before discussing either option.


## Administration and Format Considerations


Format is one of the more practical differences between these two treatment categories. One treatment category is available only as an injection, while the other offers an oral option in addition to an injection, giving patients an additional format to discuss. Neither format is inherently easier to manage than the other: comfort with self-injection and tolerance for a daily pill both vary from person to person. Storage, handling, and administration instructions differ by product and come directly from the dispensing pharmacy, so patients should follow the guidance included with their specific prescription instead of general assumptions found online. A licensed healthcare provider factors format preference in alongside medical history and other health details when discussing which option may fit a patient's routine.


## Side Effects and Safety Considerations


### Common Digestive Side Effects


Both treatment categories share a similar side effect pattern, since each works through related digestive and appetite pathways. Nausea, diarrhea, constipation, and vomiting are the most commonly reported effects, particularly when a dose is increased: a pattern covered in detail in a[week-by-week GLP-1 side effects guide](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/glp1-semaglutide-side-effects-week-week) . These effects often ease as the body adjusts, though this varies from person to person.


### Boxed Warning and Contraindications


Beyond digestive symptoms, both treatment categories carry a Serious Warnings and Precautions notice in their Health Canada product monographs, related to a risk of thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma. Both are contraindicated for anyone with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2, and a licensed provider reviews this and other contraindications against your full medical history before considering either option. Readers comparing options may also find it useful to review personal and family medical history, current prescriptions, and any conditions that might affect suitability. No treatment in this category is free of risk.


### Talking to a Provider About Tolerability


Because tolerability differs from person to person, a direct conversation with a provider is more useful than a generic list. A licensed healthcare provider can review a patient's history, flag contraindications, and monitor the response if treatment begins.


## What Factors Does a Provider Weigh Before Prescribing?


A provider weighs more than a single data point when considering these options. Personal and family medical history comes first, since certain conditions or past reactions can rule one path out, and factors like[preserving muscle during GLP-1 weight loss](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/preserve-muscle-during-glp1-weight-loss) are also worth discussing with a provider.


### Factors a Provider Typically Reviews


Other factors typically reviewed include:


- Tolerance to digestive side effects, since some people adjust more easily than others as a dose changes
- Other approved medical uses that may already apply to a patient's health profile
- Current prescriptions and how they might interact with a new treatment
- Personal preference around format and injection frequency
- Response to any prior treatment in this category, if applicable


### How These Factors Come Together


A licensed healthcare provider reviews these together, alongside lab work where relevant, since what fits one patient may not fit another. This includes considerations around[what makes GLP-1 different for men](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/glp1-men-canada) .

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tirzepatide and Semaglutide


### How do providers compare these treatment categories?


Outcomes vary from person to person, so a licensed healthcare provider reviews a patient's health history, current prescriptions, and goals before considering either option. Factors like adherence and how the body responds over time play a role that no general comparison can capture.


### Can I switch between tirzepatide and semaglutide?


Switching from one treatment category to another is a decision a licensed healthcare provider makes after reviewing the patient's history with the current treatment, including how it was tolerated and whether it met treatment goals. Any change in treatment should go through a licensed healthcare provider instead of being adjusted on your own.


### Do tirzepatide and semaglutide cause the same side effects?


Both treatment categories share a similar side effect profile, since each works through related digestive and appetite pathways. Nausea, diarrhea, constipation, and vomiting are the most commonly reported effects, especially during dose changes, though how strongly these effects are noticed varies from person to person.


### What are the brand names for tirzepatide and semaglutide in Canada?


Tirzepatide is sold in Canada under the brand name Mounjaro, from Eli Lilly. Semaglutide is available under several brand names, including Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Wegovy, from Novo Nordisk, along with an authorized generic semaglutide injection. Each brand covers specific approved uses, and a licensed healthcare provider confirms which product applies to your situation.


### What does research show about these treatments and blood sugar control?


Both treatment categories have been studied for outcomes related to blood sugar control, among other approved medical uses. A licensed provider weighs your diabetes history and current medications before recommending either option, since individual results are not predicted by any published study.


### How does a provider decide which option might fit me?


A provider looks at personal and family medical history, current prescriptions, and any prior response to treatment in this category before considering either option. Format preference and individual tolerance for digestive side effects factor in too, since what suits one patient may not suit another.


### Does Health Canada consider one option safer than the other?


Health Canada reviews both treatment categories through the same formal process and publishes a Summary Basis of Decision for each, covering safety, effectiveness, and quality findings. Neither authorization signals that one category is favoured over the other, and both remain prescription-only and subject to ongoing review.


## Final Thoughts on Sorting Through Tirzepatide and Semaglutide


Sorting through treatment options comes down to more than general information alone. A provider looks at medical history, current prescriptions, and how the body tends to respond before suggesting any direction. That kind of individual review is what turns a general overview like this one into something useful for overall health decisions. From here, the next move is simply a conversation with a licensed provider who can apply these details to your situation.
